events.title: The first World Day of Peace
events.shortBlurb: Pope Paul VI opened the civil year with a new annual appeal that the whole world observe the first of January as a day for peace…
body: On 1 January 1968 the Church kept for the first time the World Day of Peace. Pope Paul VI had proposed the observance in a message from the Vatican dated 8 December 1967, asking that the opening day of every civil year be dedicated to thoughts and resolutions of peace among nations and peoples.

He addressed his appeal not to Catholics alone but to all men of good will, hoping that governments, international organizations, and every friend of peace would take up the day as their own; the Church, he wrote, wished simply to launch the idea, with the intention of service and of example.

Paul VI took care that the day not change the liturgical calendar, which reserves the first of January to the Solemnity of Mary, the Mother of God, so that her feast might shed its light upon the prayer for peace. Every year since, the reigning pope has issued a message for the day on a chosen theme of justice and peace.

sources.text: Message of Pope Paul VI for the First World Day of Peace, 1 January 1968 (vatican.va)
